newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MoDo says profit fall softened by hedging.
newsitem.headline: MoDo says profit fall softened by hedging.

text.p: Swedish forestry group Modo AB said on Wednesday its 1996 profits fell 44 percent but currency hedging had softened the blow, with a positive effect of 1.45 billion crowns.

Posting a lower-than-expected profit after financial items of 2.92 billion crowns, MoDo said the start of 1997 has shown good demand for fine paper and board products but that there had been some weakening in the pulp market.
Modo, suffering the fate of most forest products group as the sector enters a cyclical downturn, was still able to increase its dividend slightly to 9.0 crowns per share from 8.50 crowns in 1995.
The lower profits were due mainly to the tumbling pulp and paper prices, the company added.
Modo said demand had remained strong in Q4 of 1996 although a softening in demand for newsprint had been noted. Stronger demand for fine paper which had started in the summer remained strong.
The start of 1997 saw the better demand for fine paper continue.
Norscan pulp stocks were rising in 1997 and there was a tendency towards price pressure, Modo said.
